result:
Solution 1 is not credible. A Möbius-strip graph is not a standard planar 4-regular graph, and the "50 vertices" claim is asserted without any construction or check.

Solution 2 rests on a false premise. There is no simple 4-regular planar graph on 7 vertices. The complement of a 4-regular graph on 7 vertices is 2-regular, so it is C₇ or C₃ ∪ C₄. The complement of C₃ ∪ C₄ contains K₃,₄ and is nonplanar. The complement of C₇ is also nonplanar. So 7 cannot be the answer.

Solution 3 is the most plausible of the three. The square antiprism is a valid simple, connected, planar 4-regular graph on 8 vertices, so the answer is at least a possible candidate. Its reasoning is weak, though. It never verifies that the antiprism admits a 1-regular conflict graph with no conflict-free cut, and its argument against the octahedron is hand-waving. The octahedron (6 vertices) is also a credible candidate that the solution dismisses without a rigorous check. So the answer 8 is unconfirmed, but it is the best-supported of the three options.

CHOICE: 3
